newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 27.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Early this morning heavy gunfire broke out on the West Bank close to Jerusalem, as Israel prepared itself for the funerals of dozens of victims of the worst violence since the Six Day War. As Palestinian and Israeli forces geared up for another day of fighting, world leaders appealed for calm.

In an exclusive interview with the Evening Standard, the Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has insisted that any tax cuts in his November budget will have to be offset by reductions in public spending and that a boom in consumer spending could make tax cuts a dangerous move.
HIGH STREET CHEER GIVES ENGINEERS A THIRD-QUARTER BOOST

The upsurge in high street spending is feeding into the engineering sector. The Engineering Employers' Federation survey shows that output, new orders and capacity utilisation are all stronger than three months ago.
ZURICH IN LIMELIGHT AFTER DISCOUNT CUT

Yesterday's surprise decision by the Swiss National Bank to cut its discount rate from 1.5 percent to one percent, the lowest for 18 years, has led the Swiss franc to fall further against sterling and the dollar overnight.
NEW FORD BIDS TO WIN CONTROL OF CARMAKER

Following a succession of professional managers acting as chairmen and chief executives of Ford since 1980 a Ford may again lead the company in the future. William Clay Ford Jr, great grandson of the founder, is lobbying heavily to replace Alex Trotman, who turns 65 in 1998.
